newsitem.title: USA: Santander ups Brazil, cuts Colombia in portfolio.
newsitem.headline: Santander ups Brazil, cuts Colombia in portfolio.

text.p: Santander Investment said Wednesday it raised Brazil to overweight from underweight in the 12-month allocation for its Latin American stock portfolio.
Santander said in a statement it cut its allocation for Colombia to underweight from market weight.
Equity strategist Juan Carlos Garcia wrote he was optimistic about prospects for Latin America.
The main reasons were "converging economic growth in the seven key markets", strong capital flows into the region and attractive valuations for stocks.
Santander raised Brazil to overweight from underweight. Brazil's recommended weighting is 44 percent of the Latin American stock portfolio.
Santander said it expected a return in Brazil of almost 57 percent in dollar terms for 1997.

The likely re-election of reformist President Fernando Henrique Cardoso, a reduction in taxes, bureaucratic red tape and other obstacles to doing business, and a surge in privatizations "are positives that outweigh the primary concern over the external accounts," the statement said.
Colombia was cut to underweight, or 3.5 percent, from market weight.
"Santander cited the fiscal deficit -- and the need to finance it -- as key concerns, as well as lackluster upside potential in the market," the report said.

In the rest of Latin America, Santander kept its 12-month overweight positions on Mexico and Venezuela. It reiterated its market weight stance on Argentina and Peru and its underweight position on Chile.
The benchmark for weightings is the Santander Investment Neutral Index.
